title: Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'
profile_applicability:
•  Level 1 - Domain Controller
•  Level 1 - Member Server

branching.result_aggregation: PASS if the active branch verify step passes; SKIP if a branch is not applicable to this host (the other role); FAIL if the active branch check fails; ERROR if role detection fails or DomainRole value is unrecognised. Use the DC verify status for cis_result when is_dc is true; use the Member Server verify status when is_member is true.

objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 1.1.1: Ensure 'Enforce password history' is set to '24 or more password(s)'

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Check if the server is a Domain Controller or Member Server using: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole`
steps.function: 1. Check if the server is a Domain Controller or Member Server using: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole`. Expected result: 4 or 5 for DC, 0-3 for Member Server.

steps.name: Check DC password history policy using: `Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object -ExpandProperty…
steps.function: 2. Check DC password history policy using: `Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object -ExpandProperty PasswordHistoryCount`. Expected result: 24 or more.

steps.name: Check DC GPO enforcement using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty GpoStatus`
steps.function: 3. Check DC GPO enforcement using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty GpoStatus`. Expected result: AllSettingsEnabled.

steps.name: Check Member Server local password history using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas…
steps.function: 4. Check Member Server local password history using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'PasswordHistorySize'`. Expected result: PasswordHistorySize = 24 or more.

steps.name: Check if the OS is Windows using: `$env:OS`
steps.function: 5. Check if the OS is Windows using: `$env:OS`. Expected result: Windows_NT.

steps.name: Check if Active Directory module is available for DC path using: `Get-Module -Name ActiveDirectory -ListAvailable`
steps.function: 6. Check if Active Directory module is available for DC path using: `Get-Module -Name ActiveDirectory -ListAvailable`. Expected result: Module present.

steps.name: Check if secedit is available for Member Server path using: `Get-Command secedit`
steps.function: 7. Check if secedit is available for Member Server path using: `Get-Command secedit`. Expected result: Command exists.

steps.name: Check DC password history via GPO registry using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Get-GPOReport -ReportType…
steps.function: 8. Check DC password history via GPO registry using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String 'PasswordHistorySize'`. Expected result: Value set to 24 or more.

steps.name: Check Member Server effective policy via secedit for PasswordHistorySize using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit…
steps.function: 9. Check Member Server effective policy via secedit for PasswordHistorySize using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; (Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'PasswordHistorySize').ToString()`. Expected result: Contains 'PasswordHistorySize = 24' or higher.

steps.name: Check DC domain functional level supports PSOs using: `Get-ADDomain | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DomainMode`
steps.function: 10. Check DC domain functional level supports PSOs using: `Get-ADDomain | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DomainMode`. Expected result: Windows2008 or higher.

steps.name: Check Member Server local security policy export success using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg…
steps.function: 11. Check Member Server local security policy export success using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Test-Path $tmp`. Expected result: True.

steps.name: Check DC password history via ADSI using: `([ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE').defaultNamingContext`
steps.function: 12. Check DC password history via ADSI using: `([ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE').defaultNamingContext`. Expected result: Valid distinguished name.

steps.name: Check Member Server policy file contains PasswordHistorySize using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export…
steps.function: 13. Check Member Server policy file contains PasswordHistorySize using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; Select-String -Path $tmp -Pattern 'PasswordHistorySize'`. Expected result: Match found.

steps.name: Check DC GPO link status using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Links`
steps.function: 14. Check DC GPO link status using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Links`. Expected result: Linked to domain.

steps.name: Check Member Server secedit command exit code using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas…
steps.function: 15. Check Member Server secedit command exit code using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; $LASTEXITCODE`. Expected result: 0.

steps.name: Check DC password history via Get-ADUser for a sample user using: `Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties…
steps.function: 16. Check DC password history via Get-ADUser for a sample user using: `Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties PasswordHistoryCount | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty PasswordHistoryCount`. Expected result: 24 or more.

steps.name: Check Member Server policy value is numeric using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas…
steps.function: 17. Check Member Server policy value is numeric using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; [int]((Get-Content $tmp | Select-String 'PasswordHistorySize').ToString().Split('=')[1].Trim())`. Expected result: Integer >= 24.

steps.name: Check DC GPO security filter includes Domain Users using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object…
steps.function: 18. Check DC GPO security filter includes Domain Users using: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SecurityFilter`. Expected result: Contains 'Domain Users'.

steps.name: Check Member Server policy file is not empty using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas…
steps.function: 19. Check Member Server policy file is not empty using: `$tmp = "$env:TEMP\secpol.cfg"; secedit /export /cfg $tmp /areas SECURITYPOLICY /quiet; (Get-Item $tmp).Length`. Expected result: Greater than 0.

steps.name: Check overall compliance: For DC, if PasswordHistoryCount >= 24 and GPO enforced, PASS; for Member Server, if…
steps.function: 20. Check overall compliance: For DC, if PasswordHistoryCount >= 24 and GPO enforced, PASS; for Member Server, if PasswordHistorySize >= 24, PASS; otherwise FAIL. Do not return SKIP for valid Windows roles.

steps.function: 21. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

compliance_constraints: This checkpoint applies to BOTH Domain Controllers (DomainRole 4/5) AND Member Servers (DomainRole 1-3). Detect the server role first using (Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole, then audit via the correct path: DC → Active Directory / GPO cmdlets; Member Server → secedit /export /areas SECURITYPOLICY. Do NOT return SKIP for a Member Server — it is a valid audit target.
Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
